The image description should be detailed to ensure the resulting image matches the desired subject and surroundings; otherwise, these aspects will be chosen randomly. This function is not intended for generating images from textual data. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

desc.description: A single string that provides a detailed description of the desired image. For example, 'a sunset over the mountains with a lake in the foreground'.

file_name.description: The name of the file to which the generated image will be saved. It should include the file extension, such as 'image.png'.

Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

content.description: The Markdown formatted text content to be written to the file.

filename.description: The name of the file to which the Markdown content will be written. If not provided, a default filename will be used.

content.description: The HTML content to be written to the file. Must contain valid HTML structure.

filename.description: The name of the file to which the HTML content will be written. If not provided, a default filename will be used.

query.description: The search term or phrase to be queried.

num_results.description: The maximum number of search results to return. A positive integer.

source.description: The source from which the search results should be fetched.

function.name: get_url_content
function.description: Scrapes the specified URL for textual data and returns the content as a string. This function is useful for extracting information from web pages when a URL is provided. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The web address of the page to scrape. It should be a valid URL format, such as 'http://www.example.com'.

timeout.description: The maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, with a default value that allows for a reasonable amount of time for most web pages to load.

user_agent.description: The User-Agent string to be used for the HTTP request to simulate a particular browser, which is optional. Some websites may require this for access.

message.content:
Below are two ways to create a **Google Cloud Compute Engine** instance that has an **NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU** and boots from **Ubuntu 20.04 LTS**.

> **NOTE**  
> Google Cloud does not use the term “EC2” – that’s AWS.  
> In GCP the equivalent is a *Compute Engine* instance.  
> The GPU type you’re looking for is `nvidia-a6000`.  
> You’ll need a project with billing enabled, the Compute Engine API turned on, and a service account that has the `roles/compute.instanceAdmin.v1` role (or the equivalent IAM permissions).

---

## 1.  gcloud CLI command

```bash
# 1️⃣  Authenticate (once per session)
gcloud auth application-default login

# 2️⃣  Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create rtx-a6000-ubuntu \
  --zone us-central1-a \
  --machine-type n1-standard-8 \          # 8 vCPU, 30 GB RAM
  --image-family ubuntu-2004-lts \
  --image-project ubuntu-os-cloud \
  --boot-disk-size 100GB \
  --boot-disk-type pd-ssd \
  --boot-disk-device-name rtx-a6000-ubuntu \
  --accelerator type=nvidia-a6000,count=1 \
  --maintenance-policy TERMINATE \
  --restart-on-failure \
  --metadata startup-script='#!/bin/bash
    sudo apt-get update
    sudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535
    sudo reboot' \
  --tags http-server,https-server \
  --network default \
  --subnet default \
  --no-address   # omit external IP if you don’t want one
```

### What each flag does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--zone` | Where the VM lives. Pick a zone that supports GPUs (e.g., `us-central1-a`). |
| `--machine-type` | CPU/RAM. `n1-standard-8` gives 8 vCPUs & 30 GB RAM – plenty for a single RTX A6000. |
| `--image-family` / `--image-project` | Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image. |
| `--boot-disk-size` / `--boot-disk-type` | SSD boot disk, 100 GB. |
| `--accelerator` | Adds the GPU. |
| `--maintenance-policy TERMINATE` | If the host machine is reclaimed, the VM is terminated (default). |
| `--restart-on-failure` | Auto‑restart on crash. |
| `--metadata startup-script` | Installs the NVIDIA driver automatically on first boot. |
| `--tags` | Allows HTTP/HTTPS firewall rules. |
| `--no-address` | Omit an external IP if you only need internal networking. |

---

## 2.  REST API call (JSON)

If you prefer to hit the Compute Engine REST API directly (e.g., from a script or Terraform), use the following POST request:

```http
POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/instances
Authorization: Bearer {ACCESS_TOKEN}
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-ubuntu",
  "machineType": "projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "subnetwork": "regions/{REGION}/subnetworks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        {
          "name": "External NAT",
          "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT"
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "accelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorType": "projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-a6000",
      "acceleratorCount": 1
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\nsudo apt-get update\nsudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535\nsudo reboot"
      }
    ]
  },
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": [
        "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "tags": {
    "items": ["http-server", "https-server"]
  }
}
```

### Replace placeholders

| Placeholder | Example / How to get it |
|-------------|------------------------|
| `{PROJECT_ID}` | Your GCP project ID (e.g., `my-gcp-project`). |
| `{ZONE}` | A GPU‑enabled zone, e.g., `us-central1-a`. |
| `{REGION}` | The region part of the zone (`us-central1`). |
| `{ACCESS_TOKEN}` | OAuth 2.0 token with `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform` scope. |

### Steps to use the REST API

1. **Enable the Compute Engine API** in your project.  
2. **Create a service account** with the necessary IAM roles.  
3. **Obtain an OAuth 2.0 access token** (e.g., via `gcloud auth application-default print-access-token`).  
4. **Send the POST request** (curl, Postman, or any HTTP client).  

Example curl:

```bash
curl -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth application-default print-access-token)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @instance.json \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/${PROJECT_ID}/zones/${ZONE}/instances"
```

*(Save the JSON body above to `instance.json`.)*

---

## Quick Checklist

| ✅ | Item |
|----|------|
| ✅ | Project has billing enabled. |
| ✅ | Compute Engine API enabled. |
| ✅ | GPU quota for `nvidia-a6000` in chosen zone. |
| ✅ | Service account with `roles/compute.instanceAdmin.v1`. |
| ✅ | `gcloud` installed (if using CLI). |
| ✅ | `nvidia-driver-535` (or newer) is installed via startup script. |

Once the instance is up, you can SSH into it and verify the GPU:

```bash
ssh rtx-a6000-ubuntu@<EXTERNAL_IP>
nvidia-smi
```

You should see the RTX A6000 listed with its driver version. Happy GPU computing!
